title: At least 25 active S-boxes in a nonzero four-round differential or linear trail

target.description: Four consecutive normal Rijndael core rounds on a128-bit state, with standard diffusion and an arbitrary fixed sequence of round keys. The two executions of a differential use the same sequence; different rounds need not have identical key values.

setting.key_relation: One arbitrary fixed sequence of round keys; the two executions of a differential use the same sequence. Round keys need not be identical to one another.
setting.key_population: All fixed round-key sequences for the stated structural property; product-model qualifications are stated separately.
setting.plaintext_model: Nonzero differential or linear trails on the 128-bit Rijndael state.
assumptions: Standard 128-bit Rijndael S-box, ShiftRows and MixColumns; not related-key differences.
Individual trail activity only; neither differential/linear hull bounds nor completed attacks are asserted.

time.note: A structural theorem does not specify an attack running time.

data.note: No secret-key oracle is part of this theorem.

memory.note: No attack storage bound is asserted.

preprocessing.note: Theorem scope rather than attack preprocessing.

success.description: A universal combinatorial trail-activity statement, not an attack success probability.

bound.quantifier: Every nonzero four-round differential or linear trail for an arbitrary fixed sequence of round keys in the stated core-round model.
bound.scope: Applies to individual trail activity; no claim about a full-cipher security level, total differential probability, or related-key trails is inferred.

evidence.locator: PDF29 / printed27 Section7.3.1 branch5; PDF33 / printed31 Section8.2.3; PDF34–37 / printed32–35 Section8.2.4, Theorem1, Lemma1, Theorem2 and proofs.
evidence.interpretation: Complete47-page independent raw-first read. Theorem1 gives5Q over two rounds, the intervening column lemma gives5, and Theorem2 gives25; ordinary supporting components are not separate attack points.

limitations: All47 main-source pages read; component algebra and finite integral controls checked, but no automated four-round trail search or formal proof assistant was run.
This combinatorial theorem is separate from predicted differential products, linear hulls and complete key recovery.
